key_insight: Multi-turn reinforcement learning in simulated psychiatric intake improved a language model’s interviewing, diagnostic reasoning, and safety performance compared with its identically prompted base model.
engineering_relevance: Simulation offers a controlled testbed for training and stress-testing clinical conversational agents, with gains transferring to psychiatrist-enacted encounters.
method: Train with multi-turn reinforcement learning in simulated psychiatric intake environments.
Compare trained and base models in a randomized, double-blind crossover study with psychiatrist role-players and independent psychiatrist raters.
Stress-test safety using 256 adversarial presentations derived from Delphi-consensus taxonomies.
evidence_signal: The trained agent outperformed the base model in 76.7% of 60 matched scenario pairs (120 encounters; p < 0.0001), while adversarial testing showed acute-risk under-triage fell from 30.5% to 12.9%.
watch_item: Evaluation used simulated and psychiatrist-enacted encounters rather than real-patient care; residual safety gaps require safeguards and clinician oversight.
paper_title: Training language models in simulation for psychiatric intake
